Plot size needed to detect a difference (Hatheway)

Source: R/pathology.R
hatheway_size.Rd

Hatheway's (1961) relation between plot size, replication and the difference that can be detected, from Smith's index: x^b = 2 (t1 + t2)^2 CV1^2 / (r d^2), where CV1 is the coefficient of variation of the basic units (%), d the true difference to detect as a percentage of the mean, r the number of replicates, t1 the two-sided t for alpha and t2 the one-sided t for the power wanted.

Usage

hatheway_size(
  index,
  reps,
  difference,
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  treatments = NULL,
  cv = NULL
)

Arguments

index

An "ad_smith" object from smith_index(), or the value of b (then give cv).

reps

Number(s) of replicates.

difference

Difference(s) to detect, as a percentage of the mean.

alpha

Significance level (two-sided).

power

Probability of detecting the difference.

treatments

Optional number of treatments: the t values then use the error degrees of freedom of a randomised complete block design, (reps - 1) (treatments - 1); otherwise normal quantiles are used.

cv

Coefficient of variation (%) of the basic units; by default the one of the uniformity trial.

Value

A data frame with reps, difference, the error df and the plot size in basic units (plot_size).

References

Hatheway, W. H. (1961). Convenient plot size. Agronomy Journal 53, 279-280.

Examples

sm <- smith_index(uniformity_trial)
hatheway_size(sm, reps = 3:6, difference = c(10, 15), treatments = 8)
#>   reps difference df  plot_size
#> 1    3         10 14 35.8278655
#> 2    4         10 21 15.4204465
#> 3    5         10 28  8.3095551
#> 4    6         10 35  5.0828259
#> 5    3         15 14  4.7268758
#> 6    4         15 21  2.0344649
#> 7    5         15 28  1.0963041
#> 8    6         15 35  0.6705922
